questions.q: What is the staging layer's primary role in an ETL pipeline?
options: To permanently replace the source OLTP database
To hold source data temporarily, in near-source form, before transformation and load into the warehouse
To store only aggregated summary totals
To serve as the main reporting layer analysts query directly
questions.explain: Staging tables sit between extract and the final warehouse load, giving transformation logic a safe, isolated place to run before warehouse-shaped data is loaded.

questions.q: Why does isolating the source system behind a staging layer matter?
options: It guarantees the source system never needs backups again
It removes the need for the source system to have any data at all
It makes the source database run faster automatically
Once data is extracted, slow transformation work no longer holds connections or locks against the live production OLTP system
questions.explain: Extract happens once and quickly; the (often slower) transformation logic then runs entirely against staged data, not against the system still handling live transactions.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's description of the ETL Transform stage, what do staging tables do during that phase?
options: They store only the schema, never any rows
They temporarily hold data as it is processed
They replace the need for a transformation engine entirely
They automatically delete themselves after every load
questions.explain: The Azure Architecture Center's ETL article describes the transformation phase as often involving staging tables that temporarily hold data as it is processed and ultimately loaded into its destination.

questions.q: Why is failing against a staging table preferable to failing during a direct source-to-warehouse load?
options: Staging tables cannot fail, by definition
A staging failure can be inspected and fixed without corrupting or blocking the warehouse tables that reports are actively querying
Staging automatically fixes any bad row without human review
It isn't preferable — both are exactly equally risky
questions.explain: A bad row failing in staging is contained there; the warehouse's fact and dimension tables stay untouched and safe for reporting while the issue gets fixed.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes what a staging table is NOT?
options: A table that gets used during the Transform stage of ETL
A table that end users or analysts should query directly for reporting
A table that holds data close to its source form
A table that can be truncated and reloaded
questions.explain: Staging tables carry no guarantee of being well-formed and are an internal ETL implementation detail — reporting should always happen against the finished warehouse tables, never staging.
